issues.claim: Audit body length (intro through the 'Prepared from publicly available information' line)
issues.problem: The body is approximately 580 words (title, three opportunity sections, 'Why this works', 'Suggested first step', disclaimer), well over the ~450-word ceiling. Measured by counting the body text excluding the 'For the founder' section.
issues.fix: Cut roughly 130 words: shorten each 'What the assistant would do' block to one sentence, drop one bullet from 'Why this works', and compress the intro to a single sentence. Keep the inference notes and the pilot descriptions intact.

issues.claim: 'independent research on support assistants found 8–34% more issues resolved per hour'
issues.problem: Not supported by the cited study. NBER WP 31161 (published QJE 140(2), 2025) reports a 14% average increase in issues resolved per hour, a 34% gain for novice/low-skilled agents, and no measurable gain for experienced/high-skilled agents. No 8% figure appears; the stated range puts an unsupported number in front of the prospect as a study finding.
issues.fix: Replace with 'found 14% more issues resolved per hour on average, and 34% for new or less-experienced staff, with no measurable gain for experienced staff' and keep the existing 'we assume only 8–15%' caveat, or simply cite 14% and note we assume under half of it.

issues.claim: 'Orders flow from 30+ platforms through Order Desk into Dynamics'
issues.problem: Neither source states this chain. The technology page says PDR integrates over 30 front-end platforms and uses Microsoft Dynamics ERP; the e-commerce page says PDR uses Order Desk for multi-channel order management. That all 30+ integrations route through Order Desk into Dynamics is the audit's synthesis, presented as fact.
issues.fix: Soften to 'Orders arrive from 30+ front-end platforms into Dynamics, with Order Desk handling multi-channel order edits' or add '(our read of the two pages)'.

issues.claim: 'Toronto multiplies the exception surface without adding corporate headcount'
issues.problem: Inference stated as fact. The September 2026 release says Toronto runs the same systems and workflows as the U.S. network; it says nothing about headcount at Edison or any corporate roles added or not added. The audit's own profile lists headcount as undisclosed/conflicting.
issues.fix: Add the qualifier, e.g. 'and no new corporate roles are published, so the same team appears to absorb the extra exception volume'.

issues.claim: Intro: 'how much of that four-region network still runs through a shared inbox and a spreadsheet'
issues.problem: Presented as an observation in the first paragraph the prospect reads, but it is an inference. What the sources support is a spreadsheet questionnaire emailed to info@ for pricing, plus no visible ticketing/portal; they do not show that network operations run through a shared inbox and a spreadsheet.
issues.fix: Rewrite as: 'what stands out is that new business still arrives as a spreadsheet emailed to a general inbox — with no form logic, quote calculator or client portal in sight.' Keeps it source-true.

issues.claim: '100+ brand clients, several shifts and four regions reach you through one phone number and one generic inbox'
issues.problem: Two small overstatements: the About page says 'over 100 clients' (not 'brand clients'), and the only shift evidence is a Night Shift Manager title on the staff page, which supports at least two shifts but not 'several'. The single phone number and generic form are confirmed.
issues.fix: Write '100+ clients across four regions and at least a day and night shift reach you through one phone number and one generic inbox'.

issues.claim: '20+ assembly lines' and '600,000+ sq ft' for six Edison buildings
issues.problem: The About page states '20 assembly lines' flatly, not 20+. The 600,000+ sq ft figure refers to PDR's NJ facilities, which the page pairs with six Edison sites, so the audit's phrasing is close but rounds the first number up.
issues.fix: Use '20 assembly lines' and 'six Edison sites covering 600,000+ sq ft of New Jersey space'.

issues.claim: Section 3 premise that client questions depend on individuals' memory, and 'no client login'
issues.problem: The technology page says clients 'have full visibility of our system' for order-process clarification. The audit's claim about the public site having no client login is accurate, but as written the section can read as 'PDR gives clients no visibility', which a founder will push back on.
issues.fix: Add one clause acknowledging the client visibility PDR advertises ('even with the visibility you give clients in Dynamics...') so the gap described is internal staff knowledge, not client access.

issues.claim: Minor tone: 'exception surface', 'fewer chargebacks from slow corrections'
issues.problem: 'Exception surface' is consultancy jargon a 3PL founder may not use; the chargeback improvement is asserted without a basis and sits inside a number range that excludes revenue effects per the underlying analysis.
issues.fix: Say 'more orders to fix by hand' instead of 'exception surface' and move chargebacks to a plain 'we have not priced this' aside.
